payload.question_text: The measure that checks whether a term is rare or common across documents is ___.

parts.text: The measure that checks whether a term is rare or common across documents is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The label would point to a different kind of count or score.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use IDF for collection-wide rarity. Frequency analysis and TF count occurrences; TF-IDF combines TF and IDF.

payload.explanation: This measure compares the number of items containing a term with the total collection size. TF counts within one item, and TF-IDF combines TF with IDF.

payload.question_text: A documentation analyst reviews many Microsoft AI-agent articles. The articles share words such as “AI,” “Microsoft,” and “agent,” but the analyst must identify each article's specific topic. Which approach fits best?

options.error_type: Confuses shared frequency with document-specific relevance
options.rationale: Raw frequency can show broad themes but shared words do not separate individual topics. It lacks the rarity component.
options.better_fit: Choose this for a quick clue from one item.

feedback.intrinsic: The review would keep surfacing the same shared words.
feedback.instructional: When many items share terms, use TF-IDF to give more weight to distinctive terms.

options.rationale: TF counts occurrences in one item only. It cannot reduce the weight of terms shared across the collection.
options.better_fit: Choose this when only within-item appearances matter.

feedback.intrinsic: A heavily repeated shared word could look more distinctive than it is.
feedback.instructional: TF-IDF adds IDF so common collection-wide terms receive less weight.

options.rationale: TF-IDF discounts widely shared terms through IDF. It highlights terms frequent in one item but relatively rare in others.
IDF measures rarity across the collection. It does not show how often a rare term appears in the individual item.
options.better_fit: Choose this when measuring rarity alone.

feedback.intrinsic: A rare term could be emphasized even if it barely appears in the item.
feedback.instructional: TF-IDF combines IDF with TF, so it reflects both rarity and local frequency.

payload.explanation: Correct. TF-IDF combines local frequency with collection-wide rarity to identify specific topics.

metadata.unit_slo: Explain how frequency analysis and TF-IDF identify document topics.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.

criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.
